title: Internal friction study on high-strength low-alloy steel with a low yield ratio
abstract: Achieving a low yield ratio while maintaining high strength is essential for improving the structural safety of high-strength low-alloy (HSLA) steels. In this study, EH890 HSLA steel was tempered at different temperatures (200–600 °C) and characterized using internal friction (IF) analysis, mechanical testing, and microstructural observations. The results show that tempering at 200 °C leads to the lowest yield ratio (∼0.82) while maintaining a tensile strength of ∼1159 MPa. IF spectrum analysis indicates that a certain level of solid-solution carbon, coherent ε-carbide precipitation, and high movable dislocations density at this temperature. The combined effect of these microstructural features enables strong dislocation pinning before yielding, while maintaining excellent continuous strain-hardening capability after yielding.
